summary: Grants.gov leaves opportunities in 'posted' status indefinitely, so an unsorted search of open calls surfaces records that were published years ago and never closed: the CLI must request sortBy openDate|desc, report absent and placeholder close dates as unstated rather than as rolling, and flag results posted more than two years ago.
reason: Measured 2026-08-11 for the keyword 'climate': of 66 posted results, the first row was a NOAA call opened in July 2011 for fiscal year 2012, 8 predated 2022, 19 carried an empty closeDate and 2 carried the placeholder 01/01/2099. Sorting rather than filtering is deliberate — the API's dateRange parameter cuts the same 66 results to 27 at one year and 7 at 30 days, which would discard genuinely rolling programs such as a 2020 posting that runs to 2030. openDateFrom is accepted by the API and has no effect on the hit count, so it must not be used in place of sortBy. A regen that drops the sort key restores stale records to the first page, where they read as current opportunities.
validated_outcome: Keyword 'climate', first page: every one of the top 8 results now opened in 2026 and carries a real deadline, against a 2011 record in first place before the change. At --rows 60 the CLI reports '23 of 60 shown were posted over two years ago' and marks each with its posting date.
